title: How do you connect two tables in Hibernate/JPA, and which annotations (@OneToMany, @ManyToOne, @JoinColumn, mappedBy) do you use?
shortTitle: How do you connect two tables with @OneToMany?

s1_definition.profdef: JPA maps database foreign-key relationships to Java object references using four annotations. `@ManyToOne` on the CHILD entity points to the parent — this is the OWNING SIDE (controls the FK column). `@JoinColumn(name = "account_id")` specifies which FK column in the child table references the parent. `@OneToMany(mappedBy = "account")` on the PARENT entity creates the INVERSE SIDE — it does NOT own the FK, just mirrors the relationship for navigation. `mappedBy` tells JPA "the other side owns this relationship — look at the field named 'account' in the child entity." Always define BOTH sides for bidirectional navigation, but `@ManyToOne` is the owning side that controls SQL generation.
s1_definition.analogy: Account (parent) has many Trades (children). In the database: the trades table has an `account_id` FK column pointing to accounts. In Java: Trade has `@ManyToOne Account account` (the Trade KNOWS which Account it belongs to — owning side). Account has `@OneToMany List<Trade> trades` (the Account CAN see its trades — inverse side). `mappedBy = "account"` tells JPA: "Trade.account is the real owner — I'm just the mirror."
s1_definition.oneliner: @ManyToOne + @JoinColumn on child = OWNING side (controls FK). @OneToMany(mappedBy) on parent = INVERSE side (navigation only). Always set BOTH sides with helper methods.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** JPA maps database foreign-key relationships to Java object references using four annotations. `@ManyToOne` on the CHILD entity points to the parent — this is the OWNING SIDE (controls the FK column). `@JoinColumn(name = "account_id")` specifies which FK column in the child table references the parent. `@OneToMany(mappedBy = "account")` on the PARENT entity creates the INVERSE SIDE — it does NOT own the FK, just mirrors the relationship for navigation. `mappedBy` tells JPA "the other side owns this relationship — look at the field named 'account' in the child entity." Always define BOTH sides for bidirectional navigation, but `@ManyToOne` is the owning side that controls SQL generation.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Account (parent) has many Trades (children). In the database: the trades table has an `account_id` FK column pointing to accounts. In Java: Trade has `@ManyToOne Account account` (the Trade KNOWS which Account it belongs to — owning side). Account has `@OneToMany List<Trade> trades` (the Account CAN see its trades — inverse side). `mappedBy = "account"` tells JPA: "Trade.account is the real owner — I'm just the mirror."

**One line to remember:** @ManyToOne + @JoinColumn on child = OWNING side (controls FK). @OneToMany(mappedBy) on parent = INVERSE side (navigation only). Always set BOTH sides with helper methods.

sections.s3_banking:
**Problem — The bank's trade management system needs Account and Trade entities linked.** Each Account has many Trades. Each Trade belongs to one Account. The developer initially used only `@OneToMany` on Account (unidirectional) — JPA created an unnecessary join table `accounts_trades`. Performance degraded with extra JOINs. The fix: add `@ManyToOne` on Trade (owning side) + `@OneToMany(mappedBy)` on Account (inverse side) = standard bidirectional mapping with FK directly in the trades table. Helper methods ensure both sides stay synchronized.

**What the project will show:** @ManyToOne with @JoinColumn on Trade (owning side), @OneToMany(mappedBy) on Account (inverse side), cascade ALL + orphanRemoval, helper methods (addTrade/removeTrade), creating a trade with account reference, and the importance of setting both sides.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** POST /trades with tradeId=TRD-NEW, accountId=SAV2001. Service loads Account with JOIN FETCH (account + existing trades).

**Step 2.** `new Trade("TRD-NEW", "INFY", 222037)` created — state: NEW/Transient. No account set yet.

**Step 3.** `account.addTrade(trade)` — helper method: adds trade to account.trades list (inverse side) AND calls `trade.setAccount(account)` (owning side). BOTH sides synchronized.

**Step 4.** Transaction commits. Hibernate detects new Trade in the cascade-managed collection. Because trade.account is SET (owning side), Hibernate generates: `INSERT INTO trades (trade_id, account_id, symbol, amount, status) VALUES ('TRD-NEW', 'SAV2001', 'INFY', 222037, 'PENDING')`. FK account_id is correctly set.

**Step 5.** Without the helper (only `account.getTrades().add(trade)`): trade.account would be null → `INSERT INTO trades (..., account_id) VALUES (..., NULL)` → NOT NULL constraint violation or orphaned trade!
sections.s5c_hld:
```
  ═══ HLD — @OneToMany / @ManyToOne Join (Banking) ═══

  ┌────────────┐ HTTPS ┌──────────────┐ REST ┌──────────────────────┐
  │ Mobile App │──────→│ API Gateway  │─────→│ Account Service (×4)   │  ← Application
  └────────────┘       │ JWT          │      │ Spring Boot + JPA      │
                       └──────────────┘      └──────────┬───────────┘
                           Account 1───* Transaction     │ JDBC (HikariCP)
                           FK owned by many-side          ▼
                                      ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                      │ PostgreSQL                     │  ← Data Layer
                                      │ account (1) ── transaction (*)  │
                                      │ transaction.account_id FK       │
                                      └───────────┬─────────────────────┘
                                                  │ indexed FK
                                                  ▼

  @ManyToOne owns the FK column; @OneToMany(mappedBy) is the inverse view.
  LAZY on both sides by default-recommend; fetch with JOIN FETCH to avoid N+1.
  Observability: FK index hit-rate, orphan-removal cascade counts.
  Security: row-level ownership checks ensure a customer sees only their txns.
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — Bidirectional @OneToMany Mapping (FAANG Level) ═══

  ┌─ Design Patterns Used ────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Aggregate Root: Account owns Transaction lifecycle               │
  │  Owning/Inverse: many-side owns FK, one-side uses mappedBy        │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ SOLID Principles Applied ────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  S: Account aggregates; Transaction records a single movement     │
  │  O: new child type = new @ManyToOne, no change to Account owner   │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ── Class Diagram ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ @Entity Account                                 │
  │  @Id id : Long                                  │
  │  @OneToMany(mappedBy="account",                 │
  │     cascade=ALL, orphanRemoval=true,            │
  │     fetch=LAZY)                                 │
  │  transactions : List<Transaction>   ◇ 1..*      │
  │  + addTransaction(t){ t.setAccount(this); ... } │
  └───────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┘
                          │ inverse (mappedBy)
                          ▼
  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ @Entity Transaction                             │
  │  @Id id : Long                                  │
  │  @ManyToOne(fetch=LAZY)                          │
  │  @JoinColumn(name="account_id")  ← OWNS FK      │
  │  account : Account                              │
  │  @Column amount : BigDecimal                     │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  (Caution) Set BOTH sides via helper; mappedBy side alone won't persist the FK.
  Rule: FK lives on @ManyToOne; LAZY + JOIN FETCH for read paths.
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
JPA connects two tables using `@ManyToOne` on the child entity (owning side — controls the FK column) and `@OneToMany(mappedBy)` on the parent entity (inverse side — navigation only). `@JoinColumn(name = "account_id")` specifies the FK column. `mappedBy = "account"` tells JPA "the Trade.account field owns this relationship." JPA reads ONLY the owning side for SQL generation — setting only the inverse side (account.getTrades().add(trade)) does NOT set the FK.

In my trade management service, Trade has `@ManyToOne Account account` with `@JoinColumn(name = "account_id")`. Account has `@OneToMany(mappedBy = "account", cascade = ALL, orphanRemoval = true)`. The addTrade() helper method synchronizes BOTH sides: adds to the list (inverse) AND calls trade.setAccount(this) (owning). Without the helper: the FK column would be NULL in the INSERT, causing a NOT NULL constraint violation. Cascade ALL means persisting the account also persists new trades in its list.

Three relationship patterns: unidirectional @ManyToOne (simplest — child knows parent), bidirectional @ManyToOne + @OneToMany(mappedBy) (both navigate — standard), and unidirectional @OneToMany without @ManyToOne (avoid — creates unnecessary join table). Always use bidirectional with helper methods for production code. Always set `fetch = FetchType.LAZY` on @ManyToOne (default is EAGER — a common source of N+1 queries).
